title: Magda
dek: A long-serving Pristinian Elder who first backs Hiram’s rescue, then announces its rejection, and later needs help from the colleagues who have argued with her.

facts.Record: Public scenes; later status not established
facts.Recorded office: One of three Elders in the early assemblies

body:
Magda is one of the three Pristinian Elders in the early assemblies. She can be warm, impatient, politically decisive and very interested in biscuits. Her history includes supporting Hiram’s financial proposal, speaking the council’s different final decision, and later receiving help from the people with whom she has argued.

Room for the work of others

At the early public meeting Magda asks the crowd to let Hawthorne take the notes that Melian cannot manage while running the meeting. When property ownership is discussed, she connects it to the laundry and accommodation burden on Herb. Her intervention makes governance answer to ordinary labor.

Speaking a divided decision

At the financial crisis meeting she announces that the Elders have declined the business community’s proposed support and will seek another means of resolving the difficulty. Some parts of their decision are unanimous and others split. She thanks Herb for months of feeding and housing adventurers while announcing an end to that unpaid arrangement. The scene does not prove that every later payment occurred.

Office across time

She is explicitly one of the town’s three Elders in that meeting. This historical role should not be used to assume she retains office after every later election.

Recorded scenes

  • Giving the note-taker room to work
  • Property and Herb’s workload
  • One of the three Elders
  • The Elders’ split decision

The decision she announces differs from her first position

Magda is introduced as a simply dressed woman in her early seventies who needs a neighbor’s help to rise. At the financial crisis meeting she initially agrees with Hiram: she prefers no taxes and praises the boldness of his proposed rescue. When he suggests discussing it over tea, she asks him to bring the biscuits his sweetheart makes.

The return to the meeting changes the visible alignment. Kaja supports Magda as she enters, and Magda announces the split decision declining the business offer. She then sets out the alternative measures, including voluntary reductions in adventurer rewards, instruction in return and an end to Herb’s unpaid hospitality. Her initial support and the collective decision she speaks must both remain in the account. The record does not show the intervening private argument or permit a precise reconstruction of each vote beyond what she announces.

The later meeting and the help she accepts

At the later Common Man discussion, Magda first sides with Hiram in starting before the note-taker arrives, then dismisses the idea that the town cannot manage without Zakar’s shop. Her participation is uneven. She says that a cough has stayed with her since the purple cloud, becomes unsure where she is and who is speaking to her, then accepts tea and recognizes Katherine through her father William.

Kaja proposes discussing whether the work is taking too much from her. Hiram answers that Magda has served for nearly his whole adult life and should be able to choose when and how she leaves. Their earlier political disagreements remain beside that respect. Kaja, Hiram and Katherine help her get home.

These are recorded difficulties and acts of care, not a medical diagnosis or proof of incapacity in every earlier decision. No checked passage here completes a retirement, names a successor in that moment or establishes her later fate.
